Topic: Ensure touch targets are large enough for easy interaction
Do: Make interactive elements at least 24x24 CSS pixels.
Provide adequate spacing between touch targets.
Use padding to increase tappable area.
Ensure button icons have sufficient clickable size.
Use visual cues for touch targets.
Maintain consistent target size across views.
Check touch targets on all screen sizes.
Increase spacing for densely packed items.
Ensure form inputs have sufficient touch area.
Provide minimum 8px spacing between adjacent targets.
Design for finger tap, not mouse click precision.
Include focus outlines for small targets.
Align visual and actual clickable areas.
Use labels for icons to increase hit area.
Support orientation changes with consistent target sizes.
Test touch areas using mobile devices.
Use accessible tap zones on icons and links.
Dont: Don’t use very small touch targets (<24px).
Don’t place links too close together.
Don’t rely on hover effects for mobile.
Don’t hide touch areas behind visual elements.
Don’t assume users have precise touch control.
Don’t reduce padding to save space.
Don’t rely on text-only links for touch devices.
Don’t use transparent buttons with invisible edges.
Don’t reduce clickable area on responsive layouts.
Don’t make small close icons hard to press.
Don’t put links near screen edges.
Don’t use too tight tap spacing.
Don’t allow scrolling elements to cover buttons.

SVG path interactive area is small though icon appears large
Icon inside link is large but only the text is clickable
Browser zoom reduces clickable area below threshold
Sticky footer covers part of tap zone making it smaller effectively
Overlapping transparent element intercepts touch events
Dynamic resizing shrinks target on certain breakpoints
Device safe area (notch) cuts into target area near edges
SVG viewBox scaling makes reported CSS size different from actual touch target
Pseudo-element used to expand area not recognized by hit testing in some browsers
Custom control uses margin instead of padding so hit area is smaller
Close icon inside crowded toolbar becomes too small to tap
Floating action button overlaps with other controls reducing effective area
On high-DPI screens CSS pixel size differs from physical pixels causing misestimation
Zoomed users need to pan to reach target causing usability drop
Checkbox/Radio inputs styled small but native control area still small
Gesture zones near screen edges conflict with OS gestures
Third-party ads inject small clickable elements near main controls
Nested clickable elements cause hit testing ambiguity
Browser accessibility overlay reduces effective clickable region
